new_sentences: Teaching LLMs to say 'I don't know' (IDK) is assumed to install an instance-level knowledge boundary, but the training signal is confounded: We hypothesize that 'unknown' examples are disproportionately rare-entity, unusual-template, and rare-phrasing questions; this confound is a testable premise of our proposal, not an established finding
These works report aggregate known/unknown discrimination or hallucination detection; e.g., SelfCheckGPT is a sampling-based detection method and makes no claim about refusal training
We argue that the teach-to-refuse line implicitly assumes refusal training teaches knowledge boundaries

If our hypothesis is correct that self-labeled unknown questions are disproportionately about rare entities, unusual templates, and rare phrasings, then about rare entities, unusual templates, and rare phrasings, a model can raise IDK accuracy by learning what looks hard rather than what it does not know

Baselines: base model, R-Tuning SFT, a data-quantity-matched control (IDK SFT + ranking loss on randomly paired, non-matched questions with the same example count and loss terms) to isolate pair geometry from added data, and a consistency-only ablation (paraphrase KL without the margin loss), prompt-only 'say IDK', SelfCheckGPT-style sampling threshold, semantic-entropy threshold, probe-gated refusal, and popularity-reweighted SFT (key confound-removal control)

VideoChat and Video-LLaMA integrate video foundation models or visual/audio encoders with LLMs via learnable interfaces; the supplied papers describe these architectures but do not specify how frames are sampled, so we hypothesize that such fixed-frame designs dilute sparse evidence in long videos, and we plan to test this against EgoSchema's reported failures of current models on long-form QA

EgoSchema explicitly shows that current video-language models are severely lacking in long-term video understanding capabilities, while SEED-Bench evaluates generative multimodal comprehension across 12 dimensions covering both spatial and temporal understanding

We plan to position ACAR relative to long-video systems that use memory banks, hierarchical summarization, or LLM-agent pipelines calling captioning/search tools; a survey of such systems is needed to substantiate this comparison

Compare ACAR against uniform sampling, random sampling, CLIP question-only top-k retrieval, a matched-loop control that uses the same uncertainty-triggered iterative re-answering but with question-only CLIP top-k retrieval (answer-conditioning removed) at equal frames consumed, and an oracle that uses ground-truth temporal annotations when available, all under the same maximum frame budget
To our knowledge, evaluations of LLM-based diagnostic collectives in the supplied literature do not include a falsification threshold for high-complexity cases
Run S0-S3 plus S2' (unstratified collective on structured extraction), S3-completeness-only, and a permuted-complexity-weights control on all test cases with three repeats
S3 must beat S2' and the controls on the high-complexity tertile to attribute any gain to complexity calibration rather than extraction or generic dev-fitted weighting
Primary comparison: S3 vs max(S1, S2') on the high-complexity tertile, with S2' substituting for S2 as the strongest unstratified collective baseline since it holds extraction constant
